The current run of form for Manchester United is in stark contrast to the team's performance under Sir Alex Ferguson nearly two decades ago. This magical night has been fondly remembered by many at Manchester United, including midfielder Michael Carrick, who scored twice in the match, a rare feat that still stands out even after 464 appearances. However, the current team's struggles on the pitch are a far cry from those heady days when Ferguson was at the helm. As Manchester United prepares to face Roma once again, it is clear that the Italian side has undergone significant changes since their last meeting. articles.title: Midterm Elections Arrive in United States Amid Controversy Over Voting Integrity
articles.summary: Millions of Americans have already cast their ballots through early voting, with over two dozen arrests made in California as part of a high-profile operation to identify non-citizen voters.
articles.content: The highly anticipated midterm elections have finally arrived in the United States, bringing with it a mix of excitement and uncertainty. The presidential administration has been at the center of controversy, with President Donald Trump repeatedly attempting to influence how states conduct their elections. Millions of Americans have already cast their ballots through early voting, which is on track to surpass the numbers seen in the last midterm elections two years ago. Despite concerns about election integrity raised by the president and his administration, voting operations have been largely smooth so far with minimal disruptions reported. The Trump administration has made it clear that it will stop at nothing to ensure a favorable outcome for Republicans. The Department of Justice and Homeland Security have been working together to identify non-citizen voters, resulting in over two dozen arrests in California during a high-profile operation carried out under the cover of darkness. In an unprecedented move, the Department of Justice was planning to deploy its largest-ever team to monitor Election Day polling places across the country. However, this effort has been matched by an even larger mobilization among Democrats and their allies, who are determined to protect the integrity of the voting process. As voters head to the polls on Tuesday, many are left wondering if the outcome will be influenced by the administration's efforts to interfere with state election processes. The president's continued rhetoric about election cheating has raised concerns that the results may not be accepted without a challenge. The stakes are high in this year's midterm elections, which will determine whether Republicans retain control of Congress. With millions of votes already cast and many more expected on Election Day, the nation is holding its breath as it waits to see what the outcome will be. Election officials across the country have been on high alert due to President Trump's repeated claims about widespread voter fraud, which has led them to prepare for potential disruptions at polling sites. This includes concerns about immigration agents being present or federal officers seizing voting machines. Despite these fears, none of the worst-case scenarios have come to pass so far. The administration's attempts to interfere in state elections through the courts have been largely blocked by judges. A significant blow came on Monday night when the US Supreme Court rejected its bid to force California to set aside thousands of ballots as part of a search for noncitizen voters. The court's decision is consistent with years of research and state investigations that have shown instances of noncitizens casting ballots are extremely rare. The administration's own record of arrests and charges has also failed to support its claims of widespread voter fraud. In another significant defeat for the president, the Supreme Court less than two months ago rejected his attempt to limit mail balloting through changes at the Postal Service. This directive was part of one of two executive orders signed by Trump during his second term that aimed to federalize certain aspects of elections. These moves have been criticized as an overreach of presidential authority, given that the Constitution grants states and Congress the power to set election rules. The administration's efforts to exert more control over the electoral process have been met with resistance from courts and state officials across the country. Polling sites across nine states were set to open at 6 a.m. on Tuesday, marking the start of Election Day. These states include Connecticut, Indiana, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maine, Missouri, New Jersey, New York and Virginia. In parts of Colorado, Arizona and New Mexico, heavy rains and flash flooding over the weekend posed challenges for voters trying to reach polling places. While most locations remained unchanged, officials may announce further modifications as they assess the situation. Election administrators and voting rights advocates have been urging late absentee ballot casters to use drop boxes or deliver ballots in person rather than sending them by mail. This advice came after concerns arose that recent changes at the U.S. Postal Service could result in postmarking delays, potentially disqualifying mailed ballots. The Trump administration's efforts to exert control over state-run elections have been met with resistance from courts and state officials across the country. Voting rights groups, Democrats and the Justice Department are locked in a flurry of legal filings over issues like alleged noncitizen voters and federal election monitors. Federal intimidation of election officials has also raised concerns, as part of the broader trend of Trump's attempts to expand federal control over state-run elections. This high-stakes environment is resulting in court battles that may extend past Election Day into ballot counting and certification of the results. The Trump administration's lawsuits have been met with skepticism by election law experts, who argue that they go beyond traditional legal boundaries. These experts believe that the administration's arguments are unlikely to sway the courts. The President himself has added to the uncertainty surrounding the election, hedging on whether he would accept the results in a recent interview. As Election Day draws to a close, observers will be closely monitoring the polls for any signs of irregularities or disputes. The injury forced Kaufman-Renn to sit out the 2021-22 season, and despite eventually returning to action, it had a lasting impact on his eligibility. He played four full seasons with the Boilermakers before joining the Jayhawks. Kansas's roster already exceeded the limit of 15 players after adding Tre White and Melvin Council Jr., who are also seeking an extra year of eligibility due to their own circumstances. Kaufman-Renn's situation is somewhat unique in that he has been granted a sixth year of eligibility, which differs from the typical five-for-five cases being pursued by athletes in court. The new age-based eligibility model would have otherwise seen his college eligibility expire due to his technical presence on Purdue's roster for five seasons. Despite not having played in all five years, Kaufman-Renn has maintained his eligibility and is now set to contribute to Kansas's team after a lengthy absence from the floor. Kaufman-Renn's eligibility is unique due to his redshirt freshman year, which doesn't count towards his playing time. As a result, he has played four seasons of college basketball despite starting his career in 2021. This distinction sets him apart from other players who have exhausted their eligibility. The complication surrounding Kaufman-Renn's case arises from his NBA draft status. Having been selected by the Minnesota Timberwolves with the 59th overall pick, he is automatically eligible for the league. However, this also raises questions about whether he meets the criteria for being considered a senior in college sports. Kaufman-Renn's statistics during the 2025-26 season at Purdue are impressive, averaging 14.2 points, 8.3 rebounds, and 2.5 assists per game. His likely status as a preseason All-American this year highlights his potential impact on Kansas's team. articles.title: Roxie Nafousi's Fragrance Line Alia Closes Down Due to Cease-and-Desist Letter
articles.summary: Personal development coach Roxie Nafousi has announced that she is closing down her fragrance line, Alia, due to a cease-and-desist letter from a global brand.
articles.content: Roxie Nafousi is a self-development coach and author who has built a lucrative ecosystem of products and services centered on personal development, including an app, workshops, journals, and affirmation cards. Since 2022, she has sold two million books, which has given her a significant audience to tap into. However, translating this community into a successful consumer brand proved to be a different challenge altogether. Nafousi's fragrance line, Alia, was launched with the aim of creating a major international brand that could potentially expand beyond fragrances into other product lines such as candles and incense. Despite a high-profile launch featuring celebrity events and retail placements, the venture struggled due to production delays, disagreements with a business partner, and a larger-than-expected financial commitment. The total investment in Alia ended up being £300,000, significantly higher than the initially anticipated £50,000. This increased pressure on the business was exacerbated by delayed inventory and lackluster sales. Nafousi has now announced that she is closing down the fragrance line due to a cease-and-desist letter from a global brand. The news was shared with her followers on Instagram earlier this week. The experience of launching Alia has taught Nafousi a valuable lesson about comparing her own journey with the online narratives of success, which often present unrealistic expectations and unachievable goals. Market research is a crucial step in launching a brand, and relying solely on an existing audience can be misleading. The idea that having a large online following guarantees success in other areas of business has been perpetuated by the rise of creator-founders. However, simply because people engage with your content or recommendations does not mean they will automatically demand a product from a different category. Nafousi's experience with Alia is a prime example of this. She had built a significant following around self-development and empowerment, but that did not necessarily translate to interest in a fragrance brand. The connection between her personal brand and the fragrance line was clear to Nafousi - she saw it as an extension of her message about becoming the best version of oneself. Nafousi now believes that more research could have revealed whether the fragrance category was the right fit for her audience. Nafousi's initial investment in Alia ended up being significantly higher than anticipated due to unforeseen circumstances. She was forced to buy out her business partner after a strained relationship, effectively doubling her initial investment of £50,000 and increasing costs further as she took on more responsibilities within the company. The financial strain led to additional expenses such as recruitment fees for new staff, lawyers, and accountants, which added to Nafousi's financial burden. She recalled receiving a surprise bill of £70,000 in January, which was attributed to production costs, leaving her perplexed about where it had come from. This unexpected expense put pressure on Nafousi's decision-making regarding inventory levels, with the company initially committing to 12,000 units but ultimately struggling with surplus stock and resulting delays. Nafousi later admitted that ordering too much stock was a significant mistake, which hindered the business's momentum and efficiency. The late arrival of perfumes further complicated matters, as it missed the initial wave of publicity and momentum generated by the brand. The digital landscape has become increasingly crowded, making it challenging for businesses to stand out and acquire customers. Consumers are constantly bombarded with advertisements, products, and services, leaving brands competing for a share of their attention. As a result, the unpredictability of organic reach on social media can be crippling for small businesses, forcing them to invest heavily in content creation and imagery without guaranteeing engagement from their target audience. To mitigate this risk, entrepreneurs must diversify their marketing efforts, experimenting with various tactics to connect with potential customers. Nafousi's experience highlights the limitations of relying solely on social media to drive sales and visibility. She notes that even when investing substantial resources into creating engaging content and partnering with influencers, it may not translate to actual purchases or brand awareness. In contrast, Nafousi found success by directly appealing to her community, offering products in exchange for genuine feedback from those interested in trying Alia. The initial strategy for Alia's fragrance brand involved partnering with Lookfantastic to supply 3,000 specially made fragrances for its advent calendar. This move was aimed at influencing future retailers and consumers to buy into the brand. However, despite getting the product in front of thousands of people, this initiative did not directly drive sales. The brand's founder, Roxie Nafousi, reflected on this experience, acknowledging that while it was exciting to get the product out there, it didn't translate into significant revenue. One notable exception to this trend was Violet Grey, a US beauty retailer known for its curated selection of products. Alia performed well with this partner, and Nafousi attributes this success to their niche positioning and trusted relationship with customers. This highlights that not all retail partnerships are created equal, and the value lies in aligning with the right audience. For entrepreneurs, knowing when to walk away from a business can be just as crucial as having the conviction to start one. Nafousi's experience illustrates this point, where she initially saw production delays and packaging issues as common setbacks, but ultimately recognized that sales were not gaining traction. Despite the early struggles, Nafousi continued experimenting with sampling and brand activations, hoping to build momentum through these efforts. However, she soon realized that greater investment in advertising and awareness was needed to drive sales. As the brand navigated its challenges, Nafousi recalled her initial reservations about launching Alia, citing weak sales figures from the first week. She even considered closing down the business at this point, but held on due to upcoming opportunities such as a Space NK listing. The ongoing experimentation with sampling and activations was an attempt to find the right formula for success, but ultimately, it became clear that more substantial investment in advertising and awareness was necessary to propel the brand forward. Nafousi's decision to close her fragrance brand was not taken lightly. She had invested significant time and resources into Alia, but struggled to gain traction in a crowded market. The brand faced numerous challenges, including difficulties with sampling and activations that ultimately proved costly. Despite the setbacks, Nafousi remained committed to her vision, but it became clear that more substantial investment was needed to succeed. However, as she weighed her options, potential investors approached Nafousi with offers of funding. But she chose to decline their proposals, valuing her autonomy and independence above potential financial gains. The brand's demise was eventually sealed when Nafousi received a cease-and-desist letter from another company operating under a similar name, giving her an ultimatum: sell all remaining stock by December 31 or face legal action.
